title: Code as a Resource — Retrievable, Trustworthy Corpus

execution.reason: All three implementation slices edit the same two files (.pi/scripts/corpus.ts and .pi/tests/corpus.test.ts), so they are strictly serial; concurrency would require unapproved worktree isolation.

tasks.title: Bound and Rank Corpus Search
tasks.description: corpus search returns a relevance-ordered set capped at three entries by default, with an explicit override, so retrieved exemplars stay inside the few-shot range the literature supports.
acceptance_criteria: searchCorpus returns at most 3 entries by default even when more entries match the term.
An explicit limit argument overrides the default and a limit of 0 or a negative limit is rejected as a usage error.
Results are ordered deterministically: exact tag match, then slug match, then summary substring match.
Ties within a rank tier are broken by ascending slug, so the set surviving truncation is identical across runs.
Ranking is invariant to input order: shuffling the scanned entries produces a byte-identical ranked result, including when every match falls in the same rank tier.
The CLI search output reports the applied limit and the total number of matches before truncation.
Existing validate and list CLI behavior and exit codes are unchanged.
tasks.expected_verification_state: New bounded-search tests fail before implementation and pass after; the 12 existing corpus tests stay green throughout.

tasks.title: Report Corpus Entry Staleness
tasks.description: The corpus CLI reports each entry's age in days derived from its deposited date and fails closed when any entry exceeds a supplied maximum age.
acceptance_criteria: A stale command accepts a corpus directory and a maximum age in days and reports each entry's age.
Entries at or beyond the threshold are flagged and the command exits non-zero.
A corpus with no entry past the threshold exits zero.
A non-numeric or negative max-age argument is rejected as a usage error with exit code 2.
Staleness is derived from the existing deposited field; entry.json requires no new field for this task.
tasks.expected_verification_state: The stale command does not exist before implementation, so its invocation fails; after implementation it exits zero against the current one-entry corpus.

tasks.title: Record What Validates an Entry
tasks.description: entry.json accepts an optional non-empty validated field recording the evidence that proves the entry good, while existing entries without the field remain valid.
acceptance_criteria: An entry with a non-empty validated string passes validation and the value appears in scanCorpus output.
An entry with no validated field still passes validation, preserving existing v1 entry readability.
An entry with a present but empty or non-string validated field is rejected with a typed issue code.
The repository corpus at .pi/corpus continues to validate.
tasks.expected_verification_state: Backward-compatibility tests pass before and after; the new validated-field tests fail before implementation and pass after.

tasks.title: Integration Verification
tasks.description: The full retained test suite and the corpus CLI both pass with all three slices integrated, with no regression outside the two owned files.
acceptance_criteria: node --experimental-strip-types --test .pi/tests/corpus.test.ts passes with zero failures.
The corpus CLI validate, list, search, and stale commands all exit with their documented codes.
git status shows no modification outside .pi/scripts/corpus.ts and .pi/tests/corpus.test.ts attributable to this feature.
The two pre-existing skill-system.test.ts failures caused by untracked .pi/skills/memory/ are unchanged and explicitly reported, not repaired.
tasks.expected_verification_state: Corpus suite fully green; the two unrelated skill-system failures remain and are reported as out of scope.
